recent_posts.title: Introducing Koog Integration for Spring AI: Smarter Orchestration for Your Agents
recent_posts.summary: Koog, JetBrains' agent orchestration framework, now integrates with Spring AI. The integration lets developers keep their existing Spring AI LLM providers, vector databases, and chat memory backends while layering Koog's advanced agent runtime on top. Key additions include type-safe graph-based workflows, built-in persistence for fault-tolerant execution, sophisticated history compression for cost control, and native parallel execution via coroutines. Setup requires adding three Koog starter dependencies and auto-configured beans bridge Spring AI interfaces to Koog equivalents. A customer support agent example demonstrates progressively adding intent classification, subgraph routing, durable execution with PostgreSQL checkpoints, and token-based history summarization.

recent_posts.title: KotlinConf’26 Speakers: In Conversation With Lena Reinhard
recent_posts.summary: Lena Reinhard, leadership coach and KotlinConf'26 Day 2 keynote speaker, discusses the growing uncertainty in the tech industry driven by AI, job insecurity, and shifting career promises. She critiques the hype around AI productivity, warning against measuring output over outcomes and noting that AI tools require experienced engineers to be useful. On leadership, she emphasizes that leaders often underestimate how much time teams need to process change, and that acknowledging uncertainty openly is more effective than projecting false confidence.

recent_posts.title: Kodee's Kotlin Roundup: Kotlin 2.3.20, Interview With Josh Long, and More
recent_posts.summary: Kotlin 2.3.20 has been released, bringing bug fixes, performance improvements, and small enhancements across the ecosystem. The roundup also teases KotlinConf 2026 updates and an interview with Josh Long.

recent_posts.title: Amper 0.10 – JDK Provisioning, a Maven Converter, Custom Compiler Plugins, and More
recent_posts.summary: Amper 0.10.0 is released with several new features: automatic JDK provisioning (configurable via module.yaml with version and distribution preferences), a semi-automated Maven-to-Amper project converter that handles dependencies, BOMs, repositories, and plugins, and support for third-party Kotlin compiler plugins. IDE improvements include a reworked run configuration UX, run gutters for native apps, better JUnit 5 test names, Ktor plugin assistance, and JVM profiling support in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate. Default versions for Kotlin, Compose, Ktor, Spring Boot, and other toolchains have also been updated.

recent_posts.title: KotlinConf 2026: Talks to Help You Navigate the Schedule
recent_posts.summary: The full KotlinConf 2026 schedule is now live. JetBrains has curated a selection of recommended talks across five tracks to help attendees plan their time. Intermediate sessions cover language evolution, data science with Kotlin tools, terminal APIs, and AI-powered Compose Multiplatform apps. Advanced sessions dive into compiler internals, object locality design, Kotlin/Native multi-binary architectures, and OkHttp internals. Multiplatform talks include Compose Multiplatform updates, Sony's six-year KMP journey, Swift Export progress, and Kotlin/Wasm full-stack development. Server-side sessions feature Google Search's coroutine-based streaming systems, Uber's Kotlin adoption in a Java monorepo, and Kotlin in payment platforms. AI sessions cover Eval-Driven Development for agents, Koog 1.0.0-RC for production agents, and improving AI-generated Kotlin code quality.

recent_posts.title: Google Summer of Code 2026 Is Here: Contribute to Kotlin
recent_posts.summary: The Kotlin Foundation is participating in Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 2026, offering students and eligible contributors the chance to work on real Kotlin open-source projects with mentorship from experienced engineers. Four projects are available this year: a Kotlin Compiler Fuzzer, Swift-to-Kotlin interop proof of concept, tail call support in Kotlin/Wasm, and a Kotlin Education landscape report. The contributor application period runs until March 31, with coding starting May 25. Non-students can also explore the Kotlin Ecosystem Mentorship Program.

recent_posts.title: Kotlin 2.3.20 Released
recent_posts.summary: Kotlin 2.3.20 is now available with several notable improvements: Gradle 9.3.0 compatibility and Build Tools API enabled by default for Kotlin/JVM, simplified Maven project setup, Lombok plugin promoted to Alpha with improved JPA support, name-based destructuring declarations in the language, a new API for immutable Map.Entry copies in the standard library, and a new interoperability mode for C and Objective-C libraries in Kotlin/Native. The release is bundled with the latest IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio versions.

recent_posts.title: KotlinConf 2026 attendee guide for Munich
recent_posts.summary: A guide for KotlinConf'26 attendees in Munich covering 15 tips across before, during, and after the conference. Tips include early registration to skip lines, attending hands-on workshops on May 20 (covering Compose Multiplatform, Kotlin Multiplatform, Coroutines, Spring Boot, AI Agents, and Functional Kotlin), catching the keynotes, joining the coding challenge, exploring the expo, attending the evening party, participating in a time capsule activity, the inaugural Golden Kodee Awards, and leaving session feedback.

recent_posts.title: How to Avoid Common Pitfalls With JPA and Kotlin
recent_posts.summary: Jakarta Persistence (JPA) was designed for Java, creating friction with Kotlin's defaults like final classes, immutable properties, and null safety. To build reliable persistence layers, avoid data classes for entities, use regular open classes with mutable properties, configure the no-arg and all-open compiler plugins, stick to field-based access, and make all entity fields nullable (including primary keys with generated values). Default values in constructors won't apply when loading from the database. Kotlin 2.2 improves annotation placement, and IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 will detect these issues automatically with inspections and quick-fixes.

recent_posts.title: Advent of Code 2025 in Kotlin: Puzzles, Prizes, and Community
recent_posts.summary: JetBrains wrapped up Advent of Code 2025 with Kotlin-focused participation, featuring five days of livestreams with Sebastian Aigner solving puzzles live. Nine winners were announced across three categories: Fastest to Solve (top leaderboard performers), Random (lottery-style selection), and Community (recognizing active helpers in the Kotlin Slack channel). The puzzles remain available year-round, with resources including YouTube recordings, previous years' solutions, and Kotlin Notebooks tutorials for continued learning.

top_posts.title: Celebrating Kotlin 2.0: Fast, Smart, and Multiplatform
top_posts.summary: Kotlin 2.0 is released with a stable K2 compiler, multiplatform support, and improved code analysis. It has gained popularity among developers and major companies like AWS, Adobe, Atlassian, and Google. Kotlin Multiplatform allows sharing code across various platforms and has seen significant adoption. The release introduces the K2 compiler, which unifies all platforms and improves compilation speed. IntelliJ IDEA's K2 mode offers faster code highlighting and completion. The new compiler understands code better and introduces new features. Kotlin 2.0 is a high-quality release focused on data recognition, abstraction, high-performance code, and library author experience.

top_posts.title: Introducing Kotlin Notebook
top_posts.summary: Kotlin Notebook is an interactive tool that allows you to combine code, visualizations, and text in a single document. In notebooks, you can write and run code snippets (cells), view the results, and document your thought process all in one place. This post will offer insight into the plugin’s functionality and use cases.

top_posts.title: Kotlin 2.0.20 Released
top_posts.summary: Kotlin 2.0.20 has been released, introducing performance improvements and bug fixes from Kotlin 2.0.0. Key updates include changes to the data class copy function's visibility, new static accessors for source sets in multiplatform projects, and concurrent marking in Kotlin/Native's garbage collector. Support for Gradle versions 8.6-8.8 and UUIDs in the common Kotlin standard library is also added. The Compose compiler has been updated, and Kotlin is now bundled with IntelliJ IDEA 2023.3 and Android Studio Iguana Canary 15.

top_posts.title: Kotlin Multiplatform Is Stable and Production-Ready
top_posts.summary: Kotlin Multiplatform is now stable and ready for production use. It allows developers to share code across platforms while retaining native benefits. Many prominent companies have been using Kotlin Multiplatform, including Netflix and McDonald's. The technology offers strict compatibility guarantees, better build setup user experience, and build and runtime performance improvements. The growing Kotlin Multiplatform ecosystem provides diverse tools for app development. Compose Multiplatform, a declarative cross-platform UI framework, offers full code-sharing flexibility. JetBrains continues to enhance multiplatform development with future updates and announcements.

top_posts.title: The Ktor Roadmap for 2024
top_posts.summary: Ktor has released its roadmap for 2024, which includes new features like OpenTelemetry plugins, gRPC-based services, migration to Kotlinx-io, support for managed transactions, and simplified dependency injection. The documentation will be improved with enhanced tutorials, cloud deployment topics, a guide on full-stack development with Kotlin Multiplatform, and increased API coverage. A plugin registry will be introduced to accept third-party Ktor plugins, and a command line tool will be published.
